name: brihat_ank_tak
doc: brihat_ank_tak(x, n, base, out) — render n-digit bigint x in `base` into pankti `out` as digit values (MSB first). Returns digit count. Caller allocates out with >= 4*n cells (70 cells sufficed for n <= 21 in base 2; n >= 22 overflowed the internal buffer). Base outside 2..16: returns 0 (base 0 trapped with SIGFPE).

name: brihat_ank_se
doc: brihat_ank_se(d, count, base, x, n) — parse `count` digit values from pankti `d` (MSB first) in `base` into n-digit bigint x. Returns 1 on success, 0 if a digit >= base. Base outside 2..16 returns 0 (the old code accepted any base, so base 0/1/negative silently mis-parsed).
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: anukram_maap_ashtak

name: anukram_khip_i64

name: anukram_grah_i64

name: brihat_ank_se_int
doc: brihat_ank_se_int(val, arr, n) — convert int to digit array (LSB first) Returns 1 if val fit in n digits, 0 if truncated. MIN: |MIN| does not fit in int64, so plain negation wraps and emits negative digits. Convert MAX and add 1 instead.

name: brihat_ank_tak_int

name: brihat_nyun
doc: brihat_nyun(a, b, res, n) — res = a - b (requires a >= b); returns final borrow

name: brihat_gun

name: brihat_asti_shunyank
doc: brihat_asti_shunyank(arr, n) — 1 if all digits are 0, else 0

name: brihat_bhajshesh
doc: brihat_bhajshesh(a, b, q, r, n) — q = a / b, r = a % b (a,b,q,r are n-digit) Uses long division, one decimal digit at a time. Division by zero is defined, not a hang: q = 0, r = a (so q*b + r == a still holds).
verdicts: reviewed: the return value is not documented; q and r are the results and are checked

name: brihat_shesh
doc: brihat_shesh(num, shesh, res, n) — res = num % shesh, where num has 2n digits Helper for powmod. Uses long division. shesh == 0 is defined, not a hang: no reduction is applied, so res is the low n digits of num.
verdicts: reviewed: the return value is not documented; res is the result
a parameter is a list, string or record

name: brihat_ghatmod
doc: brihat_ghatmod(base, exp, shesh, res, n) — res = base^exp shesh shesh exp is a plain int and must be >= 0 (a negative exp returns 1: the loop never runs). shesh == 0 means "no reduction" (see brihat_shesh), so the result is base^exp truncated to n digits. res is n-digit.
verdicts: reviewed: the return value is not documented; res is the result

name: ganit_yadricch
doc: ganit_yadricch(state): Knuth MMIX LCG — state = state * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407 (shesh 2^64, plain wrapping arithmetic). `state` is a 1-cell array holding the seed; it is updated in place and the new state is returned. The full 64-bit state is returned (it may be negative); use nirapeksh_mulya or a modulo to map it to a range. Any seed works, including 0. Deterministic: the same seed always yields the same sequence. There is no entropy source in the language, so the caller owns the seed.

name: ganit_seemit
doc: ganit_seemit(v, lo, hi): lo if v < lo, hi if v > hi, else v. Requires lo <= hi. If lo > hi: lo when v < lo, otherwise hi (R9, F4: the old comment said lo always; ganit_seemit(4, 4, -2) is -2).
verdicts: reviewed: as ank.seemit. The comment says lo > hi returns lo; the code returns hi when v >= lo (R8-01 finding F4)

name: kuttaka
doc: kuttaka(a, b, c) -> x such that a*x is congruent to c (shesh b). Requires mahattam(a, b) to divide c. Returns x (a particular solution).
verdicts: reviewed: b = 0 (congruence modulo 0); the witness also breaks the stated precondition gcd(a, b) | c

name: ganita_vargmool
doc: integer vargit root (floor)

name: chakravala
doc: chakravala(out, n): solves x^2 - n*y^2 = 1 for least positive x, y. Fills out[0] = x and out[1] = y.
verdicts: reviewed: floor adjustment when r = 0 picks the other bracketing candidate; tests/stdlib/r8_chakravala_sweep.sm (n = 2..99) agrees
reviewed: as C5; the sweep agrees
reviewed: a third candidate m (t + 2) is further from sqrt(n) than the two bracketing ones, so it is never chosen; the sweep agrees
reviewed: m = 0 is never the better candidate for n >= 2; the sweep agrees
reviewed: m = 3037000499 needs n near 2^63; the sweep cannot reach it. Not proven
reviewed: a tie between the two candidates: either gives a valid step; the sweep agrees

name: samasa
params: out, a, b, c, d, n
doc: samasa(out, a, b, c, d, n): Brahmagupta's composition law (bhavana / samasa). Given a^2 - n*b^2 = k1 and c^2 - n*d^2 = k2, composes them into a third: (a^2 - n*b^2)(c^2 - n*d^2) = (a*c + n*b*d)^2 - n*(a*d + b*c)^2 Fills out[0] = a*c + n*b*d  and  out[1] = a*d + b*c.

name: brahmagupta_kshetr
doc: brahmagupta_kshetr(a, b, c, d): Brahmagupta's formula for the area of a cyclic quadrilateral (Brahma-sphuta-siddhanta, 628 CE):  area = sqrt((s-a)(s-b)(s-c)(s-d)),  s = (a+b+c+d)/2. With d = 0 this is Brahmagupta's triangle (Heron's) formula. Returns the integer part.

name: ganita_janchit_yuj
doc: ganita_janchit_yuj(a, b, ok) — a + b; ok[0] 1, or 0 on overflow (returns 0 then).
verdicts: reviewed: x = 0 takes the other branch, where y < 0 gives s = y < 0: no overflow on either branch
reviewed: y = 0: s = x, which cannot overflow
reviewed: y = 0 with x < 0: s = x < 0, which is not flagged either way

name: ganita_janchit_nyun
doc: ganita_janchit_nyun(a, b, ok) — a - b; ok[0] 1, or 0 on overflow (returns 0 then).
verdicts: reviewed: y = 0: d = x, no overflow
reviewed: x >= 0, y < 0: the true x - y is in [1, 2^64 - 1], so the wrapped d is never 0
reviewed: y = 0: d = x, no overflow
reviewed: x < 0, y >= 0: the true x - y is in [-2^64 + 1, -1], so the wrapped d is never 0

name: ganita_janchit_gun
doc: ganita_janchit_gun(a, b, ok) — a * b; ok[0] 1, or 0 on overflow (returns 0 then). The check is m / a == b, with the INT64_MIN * -1 case handled explicitly (the division itself would SIGFPE there).

name: ganita_janchit_bhaj
doc: ganita_janchit_bhaj(a, b, ok) — truncating a / b; ok[0] 1, or 0 on division by zero or INT64_MIN / -1 (both would SIGFPE; returns 0).

name: ganita_janchit_shesh
doc: ganita_janchit_shesh(a, b, ok) — truncating a % b (remainder takes the dividend's util_chinha); ok[0] 1, or 0 on b == 0 or INT64_MIN % -1.

name: ganita_paripurna_yuj
doc: ganita_paripurna_yuj(a, b) — a + b, SATURATING: on overflow returns INT64_MAX (positive overflow) or INT64_MIN (negative overflow).

name: ganita_paripurna_nyun
doc: ganita_paripurna_nyun(a, b) — a - b, saturating (see ganita_paripurna_yuj).

name: ganita_paripurna_gun
doc: ganita_paripurna_gun(a, b) — a * b, saturating (see ganita_paripurna_yuj). The overflow direction is the util_chinha of the true product.

name: ganita_janchit_ghat
doc: ganita_janchit_ghat(a, e, ok) — a^e for e >= 0 via repeated checked multiplication (WS3, R19); ok[0] 1, or 0 if e < 0 (no integer ghat) or the result overflows (returns 0 then). 0^0 = 1 by the empty-product convention. O(e), but the loop exits early on overflow for every |a| >= 2 (a^e overflows by e = 63 at the latest); only the trivial bases -1, 0, 1 run the full loop.

name: ganita_janchit_kramgun
doc: ganita_janchit_kramgun(n, ok) — n! via repeated checked multiplication (WS3, R20); ok[0] 1, or 0 if n < 0 (no integer factorial) or the result overflows (returns 0 then). 0! = 1. 20! is the largest that fits (20! = 2432902008176640000); 21! overflows.

name: ganita_paripurna_ghat
doc: ganita_paripurna_ghat(a, e) — a^e, saturating (WS3, R20): on overflow returns INT64_MAX (positive overflow) or INT64_MIN (negative overflow). e < 0 returns 0 (no integer ghat; the saturating form has no ok channel, so 0 is the documented sentinel). 0^0 = 1. Repeated saturating multiplication. Correct because |a| <= 1 never saturates, and once saturated with |a| >= 2 every later true product overflows in the direction util_chinha(r) * util_chinha(a)^remaining — so the loop exits early with the parity of the remaining steps deciding the final bound, instead of iterating e times.

name: ganita_paripurna_bhaj
doc: ganita_paripurna_bhaj(a, b) — truncating a / b, saturating (WS4, R24): the sat_* companion of ganita_janchit_bhaj. INT64_MIN / -1 saturates to INT64_MAX (the true quotient 2^63 does not fit); b == 0 returns 0 (the saturating form has no ok channel, so 0 is the documented sentinel — same as sat_pow/sat_fact on invalid input). Guards both cases before dividing, so it never executes a trapping operation under a trapping compiler.

name: ganita_paripurna_shesh
doc: ganita_paripurna_shesh(a, b) — truncating a % b (WS4, R24). Remainder never overflows mathematically (INT64_MIN % -1 is exactly 0), but the hardware operation still traps on MIN % -1 (same SIGFPE as MIN / -1), so this guards that case and returns 0 — which is also the exact result. b == 0 returns 0 (same sentinel as sat_div). Guards before operating, so it never executes a trapping operation.

name: ganita_janchit_nirapeksh
doc: ganita_janchit_nirapeksh(a, ok) — |a| (WS4, R24); ok[0] 1, or 0 on abs(INT64_MIN), which overflows (returns 0 then). The unary overflow the checked family did not cover: plain ganita_nirapeksh(MIN) silently wraps to MIN.

name: ganita_paripurna_nirapeksh
doc: ganita_paripurna_nirapeksh(a) — |a|, saturating (WS4, R24): abs(INT64_MIN) saturates to INT64_MAX.

name: ganita_paripurna_kramgun
doc: ganita_paripurna_kramgun(n) — n!, saturating (WS3, R21): on overflow returns INT64_MAX (factorials are positive, so saturation is always MAX). n < 0 returns 0 (no integer factorial; the saturating form has no ok channel, so 0 is the documented sentinel). 0! = 1. 20! is the largest that fits; 21! saturates. Exits early once saturated (factorials only grow, so a saturated result stays saturated).

Requires a util_chinha change across the interval, which is checked and reported by returning a NaN-like sentinel of 0.0 with ok=0. ok is returned through a one-element kosh so the caller can tell success from failure.

name: khand_bandh
doc: khand_bandh(cells, n, out) — pack a qword-cell sequence (one byte value per cell, the varna_bhed/khand_bhed segment format) into contiguous bytes. Writes a 0 terminator at out[n]. Returns n. This is the boundary helper: hand-written repack loops (one per call site, each a chance to get the stride wrong) become one call. n <= 0 writes only the terminator and returns 0. POINTER ARITHMETIC IS IN BYTES: to pack starting at cell i of a cell array, pass cells + i*8, not cells + i.
verdicts: reviewed: n = 0 skips the loop and writes the same single terminator
reviewed: as khand_pratilip C2: out[n] is overwritten by the terminator

name: khand_mukt
doc: khand_mukt(bytes, n, out) — the inverse: expand n contiguous bytes into qword cells (one byte value per cell). Writes a 0 terminator cell at out[n]. Returns n. n <= 0 writes only the terminator, returns 0. POINTER ARITHMETIC IS IN BYTES: to unpack into cell i of a cell array, pass out + i*8, not out + i.
verdicts: reviewed: n = 0 skips the loop and writes the same single terminator
reviewed: as khand_pratilip C2: out[n] is overwritten by the terminator cell

name: khand_pratilip
doc: khand_pratilip(src, n, out) — copy n bytes verbatim ("make me a real byte string from this"). Writes a 0 terminator at out[n]. Returns n. n <= 0 writes only the terminator, returns 0.
verdicts: reviewed: n = 0 skips the loop and writes the same terminator at out[0]
reviewed: the extra pass writes out[n], which the terminator then overwrites; it reads one source byte past n but nothing depends on it

name: khand_anwesh
doc: khand_anwesh(hay, hn, needle, nn) — byte index of first occurrence of needle in hay, or -1. Empty needle matches at 0.

name: khand_antah
doc: khand_antah(hay, hn, needle, nn) — 1 if needle occurs in hay, else 0.

name: khand_pratisthap
params: src, sn, find, fn, repl, out

Returns the new byte count. Empty find: copy verbatim. Caller allocates generously.

name: khand_bhed

Same length-prefixed segment format as varna_bhed (R9): parts holds [len0, b0, b1, ..., len1, b0, ...]; cells hold one byte value each. Returns the segment count (capped at maxparts). Empty separator: no split (one segment). Empty input: one empty segment.

name: khand_yuj
doc: khand_yuj(parts, count, sep, sepn, out) — inverse of khand_bhed for the length-prefixed format. Joins `count` segments with sep into a byte string. Returns the new byte count.

verdicts: reviewed: lo == sn: the mutant reads one more byte; a space moves lo past sn, which still leaves hi <= lo and an empty result
reviewed: hi == lo: byte hi - 1 is a space skipped by the first loop, so hi drops below lo and the result is still empty

name: khand_unnat
doc: khand_unnat(src, sn, out) / khand_avanat — ASCII case conversion on byte strings. Returns the byte count. sn < 0: empty output (the old code wrote the terminator at out[-1], out of bounds).
verdicts: reviewed: sn = 0: the loop does nothing and the terminator lands at out[0] either way

name: khand_aadi
doc: khand_aadi(src, sn, pre, pn) / khand_ant — 0/1 on byte strings. A negative prefix/suffix length is invalid: 0 (the old code treated it as empty and returned 1).

name: khand_tul
doc: khand_tul(a, an, b, bn) — -1 / 0 / 1 (lexicographic by byte value).

name: khand_viparyay
doc: khand_viparyay(src, sn, out) — copy src reversed into out (WS3, R19). Two-pointer vinimay, so it is SAFE IN PLACE (src == out works). Writes a 0 terminator at out[sn]. Returns sn. sn <= 0 writes only the terminator, returns 0. Before this, reversing a byte string meant a hand-written loop at every call site.

name: khand_gan
doc: khand_gan(hay, hn, needle, nn) — count NON-OVERLAPPING occurrences of needle in hay (WS3, R19). Empty needle returns 0 (khand_anwesh would match at 0 forever). Before this, counting meant looping khand_anwesh over successive suffixes at every call site.

name: khand_gan_swar
doc: khand_gan_swar(s, n) — count lowercase vowels (a e i o u) in the first n bytes (WS1, R20). Explicit-length form of gan_swar: unlike gan_swar (which scans to the NUL terminator), this stops at n, so it is correct on slices. Mirrors gan_swar exactly: lowercase vowels only, no uppercase.

name: khand_gan_akshar
doc: khand_gan_akshar(s, n, code) — count occurrences of byte `code` in the first n bytes (WS1, R20). Explicit-length form of gan_akshar; correct on slices. (For a substring, use khand_gan.)

name: khand_anwesh_akshar
doc: khand_anwesh_akshar(s, n, code) — first index of byte `code` in the first n bytes, or -1 (WS1, R20). Explicit-length form of anwesh_akshar.

name: khand_asti_sarv_ank
doc: khand_asti_sarv_ank(s, n) — 1 if all of the first n bytes are ASCII digits, else 0 (WS1, R20). Explicit-length form of asti_sarv_ank. Empty (n == 0) is 0, mirroring asti_sarv_ank.

name: khand_sam
doc: khand_sam(a, an, b, bn) — 1 if the two byte strings are equal, else 0 (WS1, R20). Explicit-length form of varna_sam.

name: madhava_vargmool
doc: vargit root by Newton's method (Babylonian), to float precision. v <= 0 returns 0.0. 1000 iterations: Newton from g = v halves the guess until it reaches sqrt(v) (~512 halvings for v = 1.8e308); 40 iterations gave 1e288 for sqrt(1e300).

name: madhava_pi
doc: Madhava's fast series for pi:  pi = sqrt(12) * sum (-1)^k / ((2k+1) * 3^k)

name: madhava_sin
doc: Madhava's sine series:  sin(x) = x - x^3/3! + x^5/5! - ... Evaluated on x reduced to [-PI, PI] (k = trunc(x / 2PI), one PI-adjustment). Without reduction the 16-term series was off by ~1e-4 at x = 10 and inf at x = 100. Exact for |x| <= ~1e15.

name: madhava_cos
doc: Madhava's cosine series:  cos(x) = 1 - x^2/2! + x^4/4! - ... Same argument reduction as sin (was ~3.5e-4 off at x = 10).

name: madhava_atan
doc: Madhava-Gregory arctangent series:  atan(x) = x - x^3/3 + x^5/5 - ... The raw series converges like 1/n at |x| = 1 (atan(1) was off by 6e-4) and diverges for |x| > 1. Two exact identities fix it: |x| > 1:  atan(x) = PI/2 - atan(1/x)  (one recursion) |x| <= 1: atan(x) = 2*atan(x / (1 + sqrt(1+x^2))) — the reduced argument is <= 0.42, where the series converges to float precision in ~25 terms (60 used for margin).

name: mala_nava
verdicts: reviewed: since R9 (F2) nirmmita(0) returns 0, which is what the mutant returns; before R9 mala_nava(0) was -22 (finding F2)

name: nighantu_kunji_gudh

name: nighantu_koshtha_likh

doc: nighantu_koshtha_likh(m, slot, cap, key, keyn, val) — store key+val at slot and mark it live (internal helper; keyn already truncated by the caller). NOTE: this deliberately does NOT use khand_pratilip for the key copy: khand_pratilip writes a 0 terminator at out[keyn], which for a full 32-byte key would land on the NEXT slot's first key byte. The explicit loop plus zero-fill stays exactly inside this slot.

name: nighantu_anwesh
doc: nighantu_anwesh(m, cap, key, keyn) — slot index holding key, or -1 if absent (internal helper; stops at the first empty slot — valid because deletion is backward-shift, so chains have no holes). cap < 1 or keyn < 0: not found (cap 0 trapped with SIGFPE on h % 0; negative keyn stored a negative keylen, which nighantu_kunjika_ashtak emitted as length byte 255).

name: nighantu_srij
doc: nighantu_srij(cap) — allocate and clear a map of capacity cap (clamped to >= 1). Returns 0 if cap is so large the allocation size overflows (a wrapped size allocated a small buffer and then wrote cap state cells past it — SIGSEGV).

name: nighantu_khip
doc: nighantu_khip(m, cap, key, keyn, val) — insert or update key; returns 1 on success, 0 if the table is full (then the map is unchanged). Updating an existing key keeps nighantu_maap unchanged. cap < 1 or keyn < 0: returns 0 (cap 0 trapped with SIGFPE; negative keyn corrupted nighantu_kunjika_ashtak).

name: nighantu_grah
doc: nighantu_grah(m, cap, key, keyn) — value stored for key, or -1 if absent (documented sentinel; use nighantu_antah to disambiguate).

name: nighantu_antah
doc: nighantu_antah(m, cap, key, keyn) — 1 if key is present, else 0.

name: nighantu_apanay
doc: nighantu_apanay(m, cap, key, keyn) — delete key; 1 if removed, 0 if absent. Backward-shift deletion (Knuth 6.4R): after clearing the slot, each following live entry whose home bucket is NOT cyclically past the hole is shifted back into it, preserving every probe chain with no tombstones.
verdicts: reviewed: i == j cannot happen: j starts at i + 1 and stops at the empty slot
reviewed: j == cap reads the key-length cell of slot 0 instead of wrapping; needs a deletion whose probe chain wraps past the end with a 1-byte key in slot 0

name: nighantu_rikta
doc: nighantu_rikta(m) — reset the map to empty IN PLACE (WS1, R19): same handle, same capacity, no leak, no re-allocation. Capacity is read from m[0]; no cap parameter, so a mismatched cap cannot corrupt the map. FULL ZERO, not a count reset: the count, every state flag, every keylen, every val, and every key byte are set to 0. After nighantu_rikta the buffer is indistinguishable from a freshly zeroed map. Merely resetting the count would leave the old keys readable through the key region to anyone holding the handle — the stale-segment hazard this closes. Returns 1.

name: nighantu_vardh
doc: nighantu_vardh(m, newcap) — copy the map into a fresh map of capacity newcap, rehashing every entry (WS2, R20). Returns the new handle. Returns 0 and changes nothing if newcap < nighantu_maap(m) (no partial copy). The old buffer is abandoned (the library has no free — same as re-init); rebind: m = nighantu_vardh(m, 32). Capacity is clamped to >= 1 by nighantu_srij. Before this, growing a fixed-capacity map meant a hand-written re-put loop over nighantu_kunjika_ashtak at every call site.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: nighantu_grah_mool
doc: nighantu_grah_mool(m, cap, key, keyn, def) — value for key, or def if absent (WS3, R19). The -1 sentinel of nighantu_grah cannot distinguish "absent" from "stored -1"; this removes the contains-check dance for callers whose default is not -1. (A caller whose default IS -1 gets exactly nighantu_grah's behaviour.)
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: nighantu_mil
doc: nighantu_mil(dst, dcap, src, scap) — copy every entry of src into dst; src's values overwrite dst's on key conflict (WS3, R23). Returns the number of entries merged. If dst fills up, merging stops early and the return is less than nighantu_maap(src) — check nighantu_maap(dst) afterwards to detect a partial merge. Before, merging meant a nighantu_kunjika_ashtak pass plus a nighantu_grah + nighantu_khip per key at every call site. (nighantu_grah's -1 sentinel is not a hazard here: the keys come from nighantu_kunjika_ashtak, so every key is known to exist.)

name: nighantu_mulya
doc: nighantu_mulya(m, out) — write the live values into out (one qword cell each), in the same slot order as nighantu_kunjika / nighantu_kunjika_ashtak (WS2, R21). Returns the value count, which equals nighantu_maap(m). Caller allocates cap cells. Before this, collecting values meant a nighantu_kunjika_ashtak pass plus a nighantu_grah per key at every call site.

name: nighantu_kunjika
doc: nighantu_kunjika(m, out) — write live keys into out in length-prefixed form [len0, b0, b1, ..., len1, b0, ...] (same shape as varna_bhed parts). Returns the key count, which equals nighantu_maap(m). NOTE: segments are QWORD CELLS (len in one cell, one byte per cell), kept for backward compatibility. New code should use nighantu_kunjika_ashtak below, which returns the same segments as packed bytes — the form every key consumer (nighantu_khip, nighantu_antah, khand_tul) actually takes. Passing a nighantu_kunjika segment straight to a byte-key consumer compiles and silently compares the wrong bytes (the R14 trap).

name: nighantu_kunjika_ashtak
doc: nighantu_kunjika_ashtak(m, out) — R17. Same segments as nighantu_kunjika, but PACKED BYTES: [len-byte, bytes..., len-byte, bytes...], one length byte followed by the key's bytes, no terminator. Returns the key count, which equals nighantu_maap(m). Caller allocates cap * 33 bytes (each key is <= 32 bytes plus 1 length byte; at most cap keys). Keys are stored as packed bytes inside the map, so this is a straight byte copy — no unpack/pack round-trip. Segments can be passed directly to nighantu_khip / nighantu_antah / khand_tul with no repacking; that is the whole point (see nighantu_kunjika note above).

name: patra_path_sarv
doc: patra_path_sarv(path, out, cap) — open path read-only, read up to cap bytes into out, close. Returns the byte count read (0 for an empty file, or cap == 0 on an existing file), -1 on any error. cap < 0 returns -1 without opening.

name: patra_likh_sarv
doc: patra_likh_sarv(path, data, n) — create/truncate path, write all n bytes from data, close. Returns n (0 for n == 0 on a creatable path), -1 on any error. n < 0 returns -1 without opening.

name: patra_asti
doc: patra_asti(path) — 1 if path opens read-only, 0 otherwise. (Open failure covers missing file, missing directory, and permission denial alike — the caller cannot distinguish them.)

name: phal_siddhi
doc: phal_siddhi(out, v) — write the success Result [1, v] into out.

name: phal_dosh
doc: phal_dosh(out) — write the failure Result [0, 0] into out.

name: phal_asti_siddhi
doc: phal_asti_siddhi(r) — 1 if r is a success Result, else 0.

name: phal_mulya
doc: phal_mulya(r) — the value of a success Result. Caller must check phal_asti_siddhi first: on a failure Result this returns 0, which is indistinguishable from a success value of 0.

name: phal_mulya_va
doc: phal_mulya_va(r, def) — the value if r is success, else def. The one-expression way to handle both branches.

name: phal_se_siddhi
doc: phal_se_siddhi(out, v, ok) — lift the ok convention into a Result: writes [ok[0], v] into out (value 0 on failure).

name: phal_janchit_yuj
doc: phal_janchit_yuj/sub/mul/div/shesh(out, a, b) — the ganita checked operation, producing a Result in out instead of an ok out-parameter. On overflow (or div/shesh by zero, MIN/-1) the Result is failure [0, 0].

name: phal_janchit_ghat
doc: phal_janchit_ghat(out, a, e) — ganita_janchit_ghat as a Result. Failure [0, 0] on e < 0 or overflow (see ganita_janchit_ghat).

name: phal_janchit_kramgun
doc: phal_janchit_kramgun(out, n) — ganita_janchit_kramgun as a Result. Failure [0, 0] on n < 0 or overflow (21! overflows).

name: phal_janchit_nirapeksh
doc: phal_janchit_nirapeksh(out, a) — ganita_janchit_nirapeksh as a Result. Failure [0, 0] on abs(MIN) (no int64 absolute value).

name: roop_ank
doc: --- integer digits (private helper) --- roop_ank(v, out) — write the decimal digits of |v| (no util_chinha) into out as packed bytes. Returns the digit count. Internal; the public formatters below build on it.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: roop_ank_aadhar
doc: --- integer digits in a base (private helper) --- roop_ank_aadhar(v, base, upper, out) — write |v| in `base` (2..36) into out as packed bytes, no util_chinha, no prefix. `upper` 1 -> A-F/A-Z. Base outside 2..36 writes only the terminator and returns 0.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record
a parameter is a list, string or record
a parameter is a list, string or record

name: roop_ank_aadhar2
doc: roop_ank_aadhar2(v, base, out) — write v in `base` (2..36), lowercase digits, '-' for negatives, no prefix. Returns the byte count. Base outside 2..36: terminator only, returns 0. Digits are written directly at dst + neg, so the util_chinha just fills position 0.

name: roop_ank_dhvaj
doc: roop_ank_dhvaj(v, base, flags, out) — roop_ank_aadhar2 plus flags: bit 0 (1) = prefix: "0b" / "0o" / "0x" for bases 2 / 8 / 16 (no prefix for other bases, including 10); bit 1 (2) = uppercase hex digits (the prefix itself stays lowercase). Returns byte count.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: roop_dash
doc: roop_dash(v, out) — decimal, no prefix. roop_shodash / roop_shodash_unnat / roop_asht / roop_dwi — base 16 (lower / upper), 8, 2, no prefix.

name: roop_ank_pre
doc: roop_ank_pre(v, base, upper, out) — any base with its prefix ("0b"/"0o"/"0x" for 2/8/16; none for other bases). `upper` 1 -> uppercase digits, prefix stays lowercase.

name: roop_pad_vam
doc: --- padding / alignment --- roop_pad_vam(src, sn, width, padbyte, out) — pad on the LEFT with `padbyte` (32 space, 48 '0') to `width`. width <= sn: copy unchanged.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: roop_pad_dakshin
doc: roop_pad_dakshin(src, sn, width, padbyte, out) — pad on the RIGHT.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: roop_pad_madhya
doc: roop_pad_madhya(src, sn, width, padbyte, out) — npad on BOTH sides; when width-sn is odd, the extra npad byte goes RIGHT.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: roop_varg_mool
doc: --- thousands grouping (private helper) --- roop_varg_mool(src, sn, step, out) — group the integer part of a digit string. step 2 = Indian (3, then 2s: 12,34,567), step 3 = international (3s: 1,234,567). A leading '-' or '+' is kept as a util_chinha; a '.' splits off a fraction, copied verbatim. Empty input copies to empty.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: roop_varg_bharatiya
doc: roop_varg_bharatiya(src, sn, out) — 1234567 -> 12,34,567.

name: roop_varg_vishwa
doc: roop_varg_vishwa(src, sn, out) — 1234567 -> 1,234,567.

name: roop_varg
doc: roop_varg(src, sn, out) — DEFAULT grouping: Indian (12,34,567). The default is Indian because the audience is Indian.

name: roop_varg_ank
doc: roop_varg_ank(v, indian, out) — format integer v, then group it. `indian` 1 -> Indian grouping, 0 -> international.

name: roop_sthir_mool
doc: --- fixed decimals (private helper) --- roop_sthir_mool(dasham x, places, always_sign, out) — |x| rounded HALF AWAY FROM ZERO to `places` digits after '.', exactly `places` digits emitted (zero-padded). places clamped to 0..9. `always_sign` 1 emits '+' for non-negative values. places 0 emits no '.'.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: roop_sthir
doc: roop_sthir(dasham x, places, out) — fixed decimals, '-' for negatives only. 3.14159 at 2 places -> "3.14". Rounding: half away from zero.

name: roop_sthir_chinhit
doc: roop_sthir_chinhit(dasham x, places, out) — fixed decimals, always a util_chinha: "+3.14" / "-3.14".

name: roop_chinhit
doc: --- signed formatting --- roop_chinhit(v, out) — always a util_chinha: "+42" / "-42" / "+0".

name: roop_sign_akshar
doc: roop_sign_akshar(v, signch, out) — `signch` (a byte value, e.g. 32 for a blank, 43 for '+') in place of '+' for non-negative values; negatives always get '-'.

name: rakh_srij
doc: rakh_srij(cap) — allocate an empty set of capacity cap (clamped to >= 1).

name: rakh_yuj
doc: rakh_yuj(s, cap, elem, elem_n) — add elem; 1 on success, 0 if the set is full (then the set is unchanged). Adding an existing element keeps rakh_maap unchanged (idempotent).

name: rakh_antah
doc: rakh_antah(s, cap, elem, elem_n) — 1 if elem is in the set, else 0.

name: rakh_apanay
doc: rakh_apanay(s, cap, elem, elem_n) — remove elem; 1 if removed, 0 if absent.

name: rakh_maap
doc: rakh_maap(s) — number of elements.

name: rakh_samroop_diff
doc: rakh_samroop_diff(a, cap, b, bcap, out) — add every element that is in exactly one of a, b into out (fresh, empty, capacity >= cap + bcap for the worst case, disjoint sets). (a - b) union (b - a). Returns rakh_maap(out). Before, the caller wrote two rakh_bhed calls into two scratch sets plus a rakh_sangam at every call site.

name: rakh_sangam
doc: rakh_sangam(a, cap, b, bcap, out) — add every element of a and of b into out (fresh, empty, capacity >= cap + bcap). Returns rakh_maap(out). R17: iteration is nighantu_kunjika_ashtak, whose packed-byte segments go straight into nighantu_khip. (Before R17 this used nighantu_kunjika cell segments plus a khand_bandh per segment; passing a cell segment straight to nighantu_khip compiled fine and silently compared the wrong bytes.)

name: rakh_sampat
doc: rakh_sampat(a, cap, b, bcap, out) — add every element of a that is also in b into out (fresh, empty, capacity >= min(cap, bcap)). Returns rakh_maap(out).

name: rakh_bhed
doc: rakh_bhed(a, cap, b, bcap, out) — add every element of a that is NOT in b into out (fresh, empty, capacity >= cap). Returns rakh_maap(out).

name: rakh_vardh
doc: rakh_vardh(s, newcap) — copy the set into a fresh set of capacity newcap (WS2, R20). A set IS a map, so this is nighantu_vardh's copy with the same all-or-nothing rule: returns the new handle, or 0 if newcap < rakh_maap(s). Rebind: s = rakh_vardh(s, 32).

name: rakh_rikta
doc: rakh_rikta(s) — reset the set to empty in place (WS2, R19): same handle, same capacity. A set IS a map, so this is nighantu_rikta's full zero (count, state, keylens, vals, key bytes) with no stale elements readable afterwards. Returns 1.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: rakh_sam
doc: rakh_sam(a, cap, b, bcap) — 1 if a and b hold exactly the same elements, else 0 (WS3, R19). Both subset checks in one call; two empty sets are equal. Before this, the caller wrote both rakh_asti_upasamuh calls by hand.

name: rakh_asti_upasamuh
doc: rakh_asti_upasamuh(a, cap, b, bcap) — 1 if every element of a is in b, else 0. Empty a is a subset of everything.

name: rakh_tak_mala
doc: rakh_tak_mala(s, cap, out) — write the set's elements into out in length-prefixed form [len0, b0, b1, ..., len1, b0, ...] (same shape as nighantu_kunjika / khand_bhed parts), SORTED lexicographically by byte value (khand_tul), so output is deterministic regardless of insertion order or hash layout. Returns the element count.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: suchi_srij
doc: suchi_srij(cap) — allocate an empty list. cap clamped to >= 1. Returns the list handle, or 0 on allocation failure — including a cap so large the data size overflows (a wrapped size returned a handle whose data pointer was bogus, segfaulting on push).

name: suchi_vardh
doc: suchi_vardh(l) — private helper: dvigun l's capacity, copying the data. Returns 1 ok / 0 allocation failure (list unchanged).
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: suchi_khip
doc: suchi_khip(l, v) — append v. Returns 1 ok / 0 allocation failure.

name: suchi_grah
doc: suchi_grah(l, i) — element i, or 0 if i is out of bounds.

name: suchi_sangrah
doc: suchi_sangrah(l, i, v) — set element i. Returns 1 ok / 0 out of bounds.

name: suchi_maap
doc: suchi_maap(l) — element count.

name: suchi_nivesh
doc: suchi_nivesh(l, i, v) — insert v before index i (i == len appends). Returns 1 ok / 0 out of bounds or allocation failure.

name: suchi_apanay
doc: suchi_apanay(l, i) — remove element i, shifting the rest left. Returns 1 ok / 0 out of bounds.
verdicts: reviewed: the extra pass copies d[len] into d[len - 1], which is past the new length; d[len] is read one cell past the length (past the block only when the list is full). Nothing reads either cell

name: suchi_vinimay
doc: suchi_vinimay(l, i, j) — vinimay elements i and j (WS2, R20). Returns 1 ok / 0 if either index is out of bounds (then nothing changes). Before this, swapping meant a temp variable plus two suchi_sangrah calls at every call site.

name: suchi_viparyay
doc: suchi_viparyay(l) — reverse the list in place (WS3, R20). Two-pointer vinimay, same shape as khand_viparyay. Returns 1. Before this, reversing a list meant a hand-written two-index loop at every call site.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: suchi_shreni
doc: suchi_shreni(l) — sort the list in place, ascending (WS2, R21). Merge sort (O(n log n)) over the list's data array. Before this, sorting a list meant `ayojan sort` plus a hand-written `mil_shreni(l[2], suchi_maap(l))` at every call site. Returns 1.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: suchi_laghu
doc: suchi_laghu(l, ok) — smallest element (WS2, R21); ok[0] 1, or 0 if the list is empty (returns 0 then). Before this, the caller wrote the min loop by hand or called sort.smlib's laghu on l[2] — which reads a stale cell on an empty list. The empty check here is the point.

name: suchi_adhik
doc: suchi_adhik(l, ok) — largest element (WS2, R21); ok[0] 1, or 0 if the list is empty (returns 0 then). See suchi_laghu.

name: suchi_yog
doc: suchi_yog(l) — sum of the elements (WS2, R21); 0 for an empty list (well-defined, no ok channel needed). Before this, the caller wrote the sum loop by hand or called sort.smlib's yog on l[2].

name: suchi_gan
doc: suchi_gan(l, v) — number of occurrences of v (WS2, R21). Before this, the caller wrote the count loop by hand or called sort.smlib's gan on l[2].

name: suchi_anwesh
doc: suchi_anwesh(l, v) — first index of v, or -1 (WS2, R23). List-shaped form of sort.smlib's anwesh_sarak; before, the caller called anwesh_sarak(l[2], suchi_maap(l), v) by hand.

name: suchi_asti_sorted
doc: suchi_asti_sorted(l) — 1 if the elements are in non-decreasing order, else 0; empty and single-element lists are sorted (WS2, R23). List-shaped form of sort.smlib's asti_sorted.

name: suchi_dwi_anwesh
doc: suchi_dwi_anwesh(l, v) — index of v in a SORTED list, or -1 (WS2, R23). List-shaped form of sort.smlib's dwi_anwesh. The caller must sort first (suchi_shreni); on an unsorted list the result is undefined, exactly as with dwi_anwesh.

name: suchi_rikta
doc: suchi_rikta(l) — empty the list, keeping the allocated capacity. R19: also ZEROES the data cells (was: len reset only). The old elements were reachable after a clear to anyone reading the data array through l[2], so a len-only reset left stale values readable — the same hazard nighantu_rikta closes. Capacity never shrinks. Returns 1.

name: suchi_antah
doc: suchi_antah(l, v) — 1 if any element equals v, else 0.

name: suchi_kramank
doc: suchi_kramank(l, v) — first index with value v, or -1 if absent.

name: chay_khip
doc: chay_khip(l, v) — push v. Returns 1 ok / 0 allocation failure.

name: chay_apanay
doc: chay_apanay(l, ok) — pop the top value; sets ok[0] to 1 on success, 0 when the stack is empty (returns 0 then).

name: chay_avalok
doc: chay_avalok(l, ok) — top value without removing it; ok[0] 1/0.

name: chay_rikta
doc: chay_rikta(l) — 1 if the stack is empty, else 0.

name: avali_srij
doc: avali_srij(cap) — allocate an empty queue. cap clamped to >= 1. Returns the queue handle, or 0 on allocation failure — including a cap so large the data size overflows (as suchi_srij).

name: avali_pravesh
doc: avali_pravesh(q, v) — append v at the tail. Returns 1 ok / 0 allocation failure.
verdicts: reviewed: the extra cell copied into the new block is at the tail, which the new value overwrites at once

name: avali_nishkas
doc: avali_nishkas(q, ok) — remove and return the front value; sets ok[0] to 1 on success, 0 when the queue is empty (returns 0 then).

name: avali_avalok
doc: avali_avalok(q, ok) — front value without removing it; ok[0] 1/0.

name: avali_tak_mala
doc: avali_tak_mala(q, out) — write the queue's elements into out in logical (FIFO) order, one qword cell each, WITHOUT mutating the queue (WS2, R23). Returns avali_maap(q). Caller allocates cap cells. Before, reading a queue non-destructively meant a hand-rolled ring scan with (head + k) % cap arithmetic at every call site, or dequeuing everything (which destroys the queue).

name: avali_antah
doc: avali_antah(q, v) — 1 if v is in the queue, else 0 (WS2, R21). Scans the ring WITHOUT mutating it (no dequeue loop). Before this, the caller hand-rolled the ring scan with (head + k) % cap arithmetic at every call site — the same hazard suchi_antah already removed for lists.

name: avali_rikta
doc: avali_rikta(q) — empty the queue in place (WS2, R19): same handle, same capacity, head reset to 0, and the ring data ZEROED — the dequeued dead space held stale values readable through q[2], the same hazard nighantu_rikta/suchi_rikta close. Capacity never shrinks. Returns 1.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: avali_shunya
doc: avali_shunya(q) — 1 if the queue is empty, else 0.

name: avali_maap
doc: avali_maap(q) — element count.

name: ank_tak_varna
doc: ank_tak_varna(n, out) — write decimal representation of int n into pankti out as character codes. Returns the character count (excluding terminator). out[ count ] is set to 0 as a terminator. Caller allocates >= 22 cells.

name: varna_tak_ank
doc: varna_tak_ank(buf, n) — parse first n character codes of pankti buf as a decimal integer. Leading '-' negates. Returns the value; sets ok[0] to 1 on success, 0 on malformed input (ok is a 1-cell pankti).

name: ank_tak_aadhar_varna
doc: ank_tak_aadhar_varna(n, base, out) — write n in `base` (2/8/10/16) into out as character codes (0-9, a-f). Returns count. No util_chinha handling; n >= 0. Base outside 2..36: terminator only, returns 0 (base 0 trapped with SIGFPE, base 1 looped forever past the buffer).

name: varna_tak_ank_aadhar
doc: varna_tak_ank_aadhar(buf, n, base, ok) — parse first n char codes of buf in `base` (2/8/10/16). Sets ok[0]. Returns value.

name: pad_vam
doc: pad_vam(out, count, width, fill) — left-pad the `count` character codes in pankti `out` to `width` using fill character code `fill`, in place. Returns the new count (width if width > count, else count). Caller must allocate >= width cells.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: varna_tak_dashm
doc: varna_tak_dashm(buf, n, ok): parse a decimal float from a byte string. Grammar: [-] digits [. digits] [(e|E) [-] digits]; at least one digit in the integer or fraction part. No leading/trailing whitespace, no '+', no "inf"/"nan" — those are ok = 0 (same conventions as varna_tak_ank). On success ok[0] = 1 and the dasham value is returned. On malformed input or overflow (|value| > ~1.8e308) ok[0] = 0 and the return is 0.0. Extreme underflow returns 0.0 with ok[0] = 1 (as strtod does). Mantissa is accumulated in int64 (up to 18 significant digits); further digits only move the decimal exponent.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: gan_swar

name: varna_sam
verdicts: reviewed: the extra pass compares the two terminators, both 0

name: varna_anwesh
doc: varna_anwesh(hay, hn, needle, nn) — index of first occurrence of needle in hay, or -1. Empty needle matches at 0. Negative needle length is invalid: -1 (the old code treated it as empty, matching at 0).

name: varna_antah
doc: varna_antah(hay, hn, needle, nn) — 1 if needle occurs in hay, else 0.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: varna_pratisthap
params: src, sn, find, fn, repl, out
doc: varna_pratisthap(src, sn, find, fn, repl, out) — copy src to out, replacing every (non-overlapping) occurrence of find with repl. repl is 0-terminated (its length is derived) — repl cannot be a slice; copy the slice into a terminated cell array first (see strb.smlib header, slice-boundary rules). Returns the new count. Caller allocates generously.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: varna_bhed
params: src, sn, sep, sepn, parts, maxparts
doc: varna_bhed(src, sn, sep, sepn, parts, maxparts) — split src on sep. parts is a flat buffer holding length-prefixed segments: [len0, c0, c1, ..., len1, c0, ...] To recover segment i: walk from parts[0], skipping (1 + len) cells per segment; the length is at the segment's start. Returns segment count (capped at maxparts). Empty separator: no split (one segment).

name: varna_yuj
doc: varna_yuj(parts, count, sep, sepn, out) — inverse of varna_bhed for the length-prefixed format. Joins `count` segments with sep. Returns new count.

name: varna_chhid
doc: varna_chhid(src, sn, out) — strip leading/trailing ASCII spaces (32). Returns new count.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record
a parameter is a list, string or record

name: varna_unnat
doc: varna_unnat(src, sn, out) / varna_avanat — ASCII case conversion. sn < 0: empty output (the old code wrote the terminator at out[-1], an out-of-bounds write before the buffer).
verdicts: reviewed: slen = 0: the loop does nothing and dst[0] = 0 either way

name: varna_aadi
doc: varna_aadi(src, sn, pre, pn) / varna_ant — 0/1. A negative prefix/suffix length is invalid: 0 (the old code treated it as empty and returned 1).

name: varna_tul
doc: varna_tul(a, an, b, bn) — -1 / 0 / 1 (lexicographic by char code).
verdicts: reviewed: yn == n sets n to the same value

name: varna_viparyay
doc: varna_viparyay(src, sn, out) — copy the cell array reversed into out (WS1, R20). Cell-array form of khand_viparyay: the same two-pointer vinimay, so it is safe in place (src == out works). Writes a 0 terminator cell at out[sn]. Returns sn. sn <= 0 writes only the terminator, returns 0.
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record

name: varna_gan
doc: varna_gan(hay, hn, needle, nn) — count non-overlapping occurrences of needle in hay, over cell arrays (WS1, R20). Cell-array form of khand_gan. Empty needle returns 0. (Pointer arithmetic is in bytes: the suffix at cell pos is hay + pos * 8.)
verdicts: a parameter is a list, string or record
